name.text: Find the value of 𝑑𝑦𝑑𝑥 in log-base-10

questiontext.text:
If \(\displaystyle y={@fx@}\), find the value of \(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx}\) at \(\displaystyle x={@bb@}\). Give your answer in exact form in terms of ln. Recall that \(\displaystyle \ln(x)\) is entered as log(\(x\)).

Answer = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We will first find the derivative of \(\displaystyle={@ins@}\):

\(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{({@bot@})\cdot {@diff(top,x)@} - {@top@}\cdot {@diff(bot,x)@}}{({@bot@})^2} = \frac{{@expand(bot*diff(top,x)-top*diff(bot,x))@}}{({@bot@})^2}\).

Now suppose that \(\displaystyle y = {@logbase(x,10)@}\). Then \(10^y = x\). Differentiating both sides implicitly gives us \(\displaystyle 10^y \cdot \ln(10) \cdot y' = 1\). Therefore, \(\displaystyle x\cdot \ln(10) \cdot y' = 1\) and \(\displaystyle y' = \frac{1}{x\cdot \ln(10)}\).

Combining both results we get:

\(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{{@ins@}\cdot \ln(10)} \cdot \frac{{@expand(bot*diff(top,x)-top*diff(bot,x))@}}{({@bot@})^2} = \frac{{@bot*expand(bot*diff(top,x)-top*diff(bot,x))@}}{{@top*log(10)@}\cdot ({@bot@})^2} = \frac{{@expand(bot*diff(top,x)-top*diff(bot,x))@}}{{@top*log(10)@}\cdot ({@bot@})}\).

Substituting \(\displaystyle x = {@bb@}\) we get \(\displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx} = {@ta@}\)
